# Water heater notes

Our 50-gallon gas water heater, installed in 2014.

## Temperature setting

Set the thermostat to 120°F. At 140°F, hot water can cause a serious scald in about 5 seconds, and young children and older adults burn fastest; at 120°F it takes several minutes. A setting of 120°F still keeps the tank hot enough to hold back bacteria.

## Flushing the tank

Once a year, turn off the gas, attach a hose to the drain valve, and drain a few gallons until the water runs clear. Sediment makes the burner work harder and shortens the tank's life.

## Temperature and pressure relief valve

The relief valve on the side of the tank opens if the temperature or pressure gets too high. Lift the lever once a year; water should flow and then stop. The discharge pipe must run down to within 6 inches of the floor and must not be capped.

## Signs the tank is failing

Rusty water, a rumbling or popping from the tank, a puddle at the base and water that no longer gets hot. A tank over 10 to 12 years old that leaks should be replaced, not repaired.

## Venting and combustion air

A gas water heater needs fresh air and a draft hood leading to the flue. A backdraft can put carbon monoxide into the house. Never store things around the burner.
